transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you too. Well, I suppose what finally made me make an appointment is that my appetite has just been all over the place for months. There are stretches where I just skip dinner entirely, and I've been losing weight without even trying. And then other nights, I just... I just pick at crackers or a bowl of cereal, mostly because cooking a real meal for myself just feels completely pointless lately.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, this has been going on since my divorce was finalized. That was... about a year and seven months ago now.
Have you felt this way every single day for the past 19 months, or have there been times when you felt like your usual self again?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't exactly kept track of it day by day. It feels like it's just been this ongoing thing, but... I don't know if I could say it's been every single day without fail. I just haven't really noticed if there were specific times where I felt completely like my old self again. It all just sort of blends together at this point.
During these past 19 months, can you recall any period of two months or longer where you felt completely like your usual self?

No, I can't say that I do. Like I said, it's all just been kind of a blur. If there was a stretch of two whole months where I felt completely fine, I don't remember it. It really just feels like this has been hanging over me the whole time.
Beyond the changes in your appetite, have you felt a persistent sense of sadness or a loss of interest in the things you usually enjoy over this period?

Yes, I'd say so. I still try to go through the motions with the things I used to love, like watering the garden or showing up to my book club. But... most of the time it just feels flat. There's no real enjoyment in it anymore. I usually end up leaving early, or honestly, sometimes I just don't even bother starting at all.
Beyond the lack of enjoyment, have you been feeling a sense of hopelessness about the future or feeling down about yourself?

Yes, I have been feeling pretty down about myself. I just... I keep replaying the marriage in my head, and I keep telling myself that I must have failed at something basic for things to end up this way. I mean, part of me knows that relationships are much more complicated than that. But... it's just hard to shake that feeling of failure right now.
Over these past 19 months, have you noticed a persistent feeling of low energy or fatigue?

Yes, definitely. I just feel so tired all the time. Even on days when my caseload at the hospital isn't unusually heavy, I feel like I'm just dragging my body through the halls. And then when I get home, I'm just too exhausted to do anything. I don't cook, I don't stretch, I don't even have the energy to answer personal messages. I just kind of collapse.

During these past 19 months, have there been any periods of two weeks or longer where your mood was so low and your symptoms were so severe that you were unable to function at work or in your daily life?

Well, I wouldn't say I've been completely unable to function. I mean, I am still getting to work. But... it's definitely taking a toll. My documentation keeps backing up, and I've had to stay late a lot just to fix things that I used to handle easily. And outside of the hospital, it's worse. I've basically let my friendships and just... basic daily routines shrink down to almost nothing.
